quotes.text: If you extract documents from SharePoint to build a perfect retrieval system, but lose the permission model that SharePoint was enforcing, what have you actually built?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames the core risk of private RAG as a single, uncomfortable question.

quotes.text: A self-hosted vector database with no role-based access control is fundamentally less secure than a managed cloud database that enforces per user filtering.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects the common belief that self-hosting equals security.

quotes.text: A system prompt that says, "Don't expose confidential data" is a hope rather than a guarantee. It can be bypassed, it can be misunderstood and it can fail silently.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why authorization cannot be delegated to the language model.

quotes.text: You should never retrieve a document and then decide if the user is allowed to see it. That decision has to happen before the retrieval not after.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the pre-retrieval authorization principle in one clear rule.

quotes.text: Data sovereignty without security is just an illusion. Where your data actually sits matters much less than who is allowed to access it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the episode's distinction between sovereignty and security.

takeaways: Keeping data in a sovereign region does not protect it: if SharePoint permissions are lost during extraction, a RAG index exposes documents to anyone who can query it.
Capture ACLs as Entra ID-based metadata at ingestion and filter by user and group before retrieval, for example with Azure AI Search, instead of filtering afterwards or relying on the prompt.
Separate responsibilities across agents, use scoped tokens via OAuth 2.0 token exchange and a deterministic policy decision point, and monitor retrieval behavior with zero trust at every hop.
hook: Private RAG projects focus on where data lives, but often lose the permissions that decided who could see it. This episode is for CISOs, architects and engineers building AI retrieval on SharePoint and Microsoft 365 data, and explains how permission-aware retrieval, scoped identity and policy engines stop a knowledge system from becoming an insider data leak.
